anchors.paper_title: Annotating, Understanding, and Predicting Long-term Video Memorability
anchors.reason: The paper proposes a new protocol and dataset for video memorability, which is topically related to the dataset's focus on movie memory but does not describe or release the specific data in on006142.

metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 electrodes arranged according to the international 10-20 system, sampled at 2048 Hz. Participants watched 10-second movie clips and reported recognition and memory status; recognized or remembered clips were replayed with mouse-click annotations marking recognition-triggering moments.

citation_details.title: Topological Bifurcation of Pre-stimulus Cortical Field Dynamics Predicts Cognitive Performance
citation_details.author: Diego Cerda Seguel
citation_details.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
citation_details.abstract: Topological Bifurcation of Pre-stimulus Cortical Field Dynamics Predicts Cognitive Performance Abstract / Description for Zenodo (Deposit Description)This manuscript presents a large-scale computational analysis of pre-stimulus cortical dynamics and their predictive capacity for cognitive performance across three independent domains: episodic memory, motor control (exoskeleton), and perceptual decision-making. Using high-performance computing infrastructure (Patagón HPC), three public EEG datasets (ds006142, ds007788, ds002680) were processed, harmonized under the BIDS-EEG standard, encompassing a total of 48 healthy subjects and 21,524 experimental trials. Spectral variance within the beta band (13–30 Hz) was quantified in a strictly bounded temporal window spanning from −500 ms to 0 ms relative to stimulus onset (β_std). Key findings: Episodic memory (ds006142): β_std predicts memory retrieval success with AUC = 0.569 (p < 0.0001, n = 6,094 trials). Motor control (ds007788): β_std correlates with kinematic latency in exoskeleton control tasks, revealing a topological bifurcation in the population: two stable and opposite phenotypic profiles — stabilization (β_std ↓ → better performance) and controlled activation (β_std ↑ → better performance). Perceptual decision-making (ds002680): β_std correlates with reaction times in rapid visual categorization (r = 0.054, p < 0.0001, n = 9,146 valid trials). Implications: These results extend the classical Bereitschaftspotential principle (Libet et al., 1983) to non-motor domains, demonstrating that pre-stimulus cortical preparation is a transversal and predictive phenomenon. The observed phenotypic heterogeneity suggests that cognitive performance optimization can be achieved through opposite strategies of spectral modulation, challenging post-stimulus neural decoding models and opening new directions for adaptive brain-computer interfaces.
